description: Add short, non-blocking visual feedback animations for each care action (餌やり/トレーニング/睡眠/清掃) in the frontend. When the player triggers a care action, a transient effect overlay plays over the sprite (feed: a 🍖 appears and drifts toward the monster; train: a 気合い/💪 puff with a sprite bounce; sleep: an animated 💤 bubble; clean: ✨ sparkles), and the monster sprite gives a light reaction (bounce/shake) for every action. Effects are driven by a transient state flag + a counter key so repeating the same action re-triggers, and are cleared on animationend or a timeout. Consumes careEffect from FEAT-001.
steps: Decide where the transient 'last care action' signal lives. Preferred: keep it local to App.tsx by wrapping the care handlers passed to CarePanel so they set a React state like `{ action: CareAction, key: number }` (increment key each trigger so the same action re-fires), then call the real game.feed/train/sleep/clean. This avoids changing useMonster's public API. (Alternative: surface a `lastCareAction`/counter from useMonster.ts; only do this if cleaner.)

In App.tsx, import careEffect (and CareAction) from ./ui-helpers.ts. Render a transient effect overlay inside .sprite-wrap (next to the existing .zzz/.dirt spans) only while an effect is active: an element using the careEffect(action).className plus the careEffect(action).emoji, keyed by the counter so React remounts it on repeat. Also apply a sprite reaction class (bounce/shake) to the .sprite-wrap or a wrapper around <MonsterSprite> while active.

Clear the effect on animationend (onAnimationEnd handler) and/or a setTimeout fallback of careEffect(action).durationMs. Ensure cleanup on unmount (clear any pending timeout). Do not block or disable actions beyond the existing game.busy gating; do not add artificial delays to the care actions themselves.

In packages/frontend/src/styles.css, add @keyframes and the effect classes referenced by careEffect (fx-feed, fx-train, fx-sleep, fx-clean) plus a sprite reaction keyframe (e.g. a short bounce/shake). Follow the existing patterns: there is already a `pop` keyframe used by .evolution-banner, and .sprite-wrap/.zzz/.dirt positioned overlays. Position the effect overlay absolutely within .sprite-wrap. Keep each animation short (~0.4-0.8s). feed should drift the 🍖 toward the sprite center; clean should sparkle/fade ✨; train should puff 💪 and bounce the sprite; sleep should float a 💤 bubble.
Optional nice-to-have: wrap the animations in a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that disables or shortens them. Only add if straightforward.
Keep all visible text Japanese-only. Overlay content is emoji + optional Japanese like 気合い; do not introduce English UI strings or i18n scaffolding.
acceptance_criteria: Triggering 餌やり/トレーニング/睡眠/清掃 each plays a distinct short overlay animation over the sprite, and the sprite itself gives a light bounce/shake reaction for every action.
Repeating the same care action re-triggers its animation (counter/key based, not stuck after first play).
The effect clears itself after the animation (animationend or durationMs timeout) with no lingering overlay and no leaked timers on unmount.
No new runtime dependencies added; UI remains Japanese-only.
`npm run build` (root) passes (frontend tsc + vite build) and `npm run test -w @ddm/frontend` passes.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/kiro-digitalmonster && npm run build  (exit 0; frontend tsc + vite build succeed)
cd /projects/sandbox/kiro-digitalmonster && npm test  (shared 42 pass, no regression)
Grep styles.css to confirm @keyframes and the fx-feed/fx-train/fx-sleep/fx-clean classes referenced by careEffect exist (sanity, not a substitute for build).
